outcome: The AI authoring server (MCP) now reports which code it runs and can be kept on the Lab's code automatically
owner_impact: Nothing changes in the Lab. The MCP that GPT uses to author Experiments validates them with copies of the Lab's compilers, but until now it was deployed by hand, so after a grammar change it could silently lag behind the Lab. Its health endpoint now reports the exact code version it runs, and a new automatic job redeploys it whenever its code changes, then checks the live server. The automatic job needs one Supabase access token saved in GitHub; until then an agent deploys it through the Supabase connector. A manual 'check only' run tells anyone whether the live MCP matches the repository. The grammar design you approved is recorded as decisions D-021 and D-022, with tickets #576 (shared translator core) and #577 (one grammar). Test now: not needed; the MCP's tools behave exactly as before.

next.text: #576 shared translator core: one parser for the authoring languages, moved over one language at a time with no change to what authors can write, proven on a corpus of accepted and rejected programs in both the Lab and the MCP. It has not started yet.

technical_evidence: experiment-mcp /health gains source_commit, derived from import.meta.url of the stub's pinned raw.githubusercontent.com import.

web/scripts/mcp-deploy.mjs: stub <commit> <dir>, verify <commit>, status; .github/workflows/mcp-deploy.yml: on main pushes touching supabase/functions/experiment-mcp/** (vendor parity check, CLI deploy pinned to the commit, /health verification; visible failure without SUPABASE_ACCESS_TOKEN) plus a credential-free check-only dispatch.

Before this change the live MCP (version 53) was pinned to baf9406; git diff baf9406..main over the MCP code and the five compilers was empty, and the live read_workspace contract equalled MCP_AUTHORING_CONTRACT exactly.
